name: Lazarus BioGuard AllerGen Suppressor
body_location: subdermal cervical — implanted at the base of the neck, interfacing with the cervical lymphatic chain
description:
The AllerGen is a lymphatic-interface implant developed by Lazarus BioGuard, a consumer subsidiary of Lazarus Pharmaceuticals, designed to provide continuous suppression of IgE-mediated allergic responses and modulation of mast cell degranulation across a personalized allergen profile. During an initial two-week calibration period, the device samples lymphatic fluid and builds a precise map of the user's immune sensitization — cataloguing environmental allergens, food proteins, contact substances, and airborne particulates. Once calibrated, it releases micro-targeted cytokine inhibitors from an onboard biofilm reservoir in response to detected immune escalation, preventing histamine cascades before symptoms manifest. The device can distinguish between harmful pathogen responses, which it does not suppress, and hypersensitivity reactions, which it intercepts — a distinction that earlier-generation allergy implants famously failed to make reliably.

In GLMZ, where air quality in the Shelf and lower Tier 2 districts ranges from poor to genuinely hazardous, and where the city's vertical density concentrates mold, industrial particulate, and food-preparation allergens into shared atmospheric corridors, the AllerGen has become a baseline health investment for a significant portion of the population. Children with severe allergies are frequently implanted in adolescence, and the device is considered a standard recommendation for anyone moving into the city's lower residential stacks. Beyond clinical necessity, it has a quality-of-life dimension that is difficult to overstate: people who have lived with seasonal or food allergies describe the AllerGen as one of the most transformative health decisions they have ever made, a complete and quiet erasure of something that once structured every day.
installation_requirements: Outpatient clinic or Lazarus BioGuard pharmacy installation center; minor incision under local anesthetic by licensed biotech pharmacist or clinician; 30-minute procedure with two-week at-home calibration period
maintenance: Biofilm reservoir refill every 18–24 months at any Lazarus affiliate pharmacy; firmware allergen profile update recommended annually; full recalibration if relocating to a significantly different environment

side_effects: Mild neck stiffness at the implant site during the first week post-installation
During the calibration period, users may experience brief, mild versions of their usual allergic symptoms as the device maps responses
Rare users report a slight reduction in sensitivity to spicy or pungent foods as a peripheral effect of mast cell modulation
Occasional low-grade fatigue in the first month as the immune system adjusts to modulated signaling
cultural_context: The AllerGen carries essentially no stigma in GLMZ — it is one of the most socially invisible health implants in common use, because there is nothing visible about it and no behavioral change associated with having it. It is discussed the way eyeglasses or antihistamine medication once were: matter-of-factly, as a solution to a problem. In the lower tiers, where air quality is a known public health crisis and Lazarus BioGuard has aggressively positioned itself in municipal health subsidy programs, penetration is high enough that some community health workers track AllerGen installation rates as a proxy for overall neighborhood health investment. There is a small but vocal community of immune-philosophy advocates — sometimes called 'naturals' — who argue that suppressing the immune system's sensitization responses interferes with the body's environmental intelligence, but this position is considered fringe and is largely dismissed by mainstream medical consensus in the city.
known_users: children and adolescents with documented severe allergies
Shelf and lower-tier residents dealing with chronic poor air quality
food service workers and professional cooks who need reliable food-allergen tolerance
anyone relocating to GLMZ from a lower-density environment who struggles with urban allergen load
parents who install it proactively before their children's allergen profiles are fully established
story_hooks: A batch of AllerGen units distributed through a Tier 1 municipal health program has had its pathogen-discrimination firmware quietly downgraded — users are suppressing immune responses to a novel respiratory pathogen circulating in the Shelf, and no one has connected the rising infection rate to the compromised implants yet.

A Lazarus BioGuard pharmacist contacts the players after discovering that allergen profile data collected during calibration — which is supposed to be anonymized and deleted — is being retained and sold to a food corponation mapping consumer sensitization across the city's population.

A character with an AllerGen suddenly begins experiencing their old allergy symptoms again after years of relief. Investigation reveals the device is functioning normally — their allergen profile has genuinely changed, which should be impossible, and the new sensitization is to a compound that does not appear in any public chemical registry.
